item.title: Ex-Sony Pictures Head Michael Lynton on ‘The Interview’ and Its Insane Fallout: ‘Biggest Mistake of My Career’
item.description: In an excerpt from his new memoir, the former studio boss opens up about the personal reasons behind his choice to greenlight the political comedy, which led to fallout the likes of which Hollywood has never seen.

item.title: We EQ’d a Zoo: How ‘Frankenstein’ Used Animal Effects to Create the Sound of Its Creature
item.description: Re-recording mixer Christian Cooke and supervising sound editor Nathan Robitaille discuss their Oscar-nominated work on Guillermo del Toro's horror epic.

item.title: How Cinematographer Adolpho Veloso Leaned Into the Elements to Shoot the Achingly Beautiful ‘Train Dreams’
item.description: The Oscar-nominated cinematographer tells IndieWire about shooting Clint Bentley's period piece with natural light and capturing images that would have never worked on celluloid.

item.title: ‘Portobello’ Review: HBO’s Tenacious Italian Drama Asks, ‘How Much Stupidity Can One Man Endure?’
item.description: Witnessing convicted criminals use boldfaced lies to disastrous effect is hard enough as a communal experience. In Marco Bellocchio's adaptation of Enzo Tortura's memoir, one man finds himself at the center of the bullshit tornado — and somehow stands his ground.

item.title: ‘Journal with Witch’ Is the Best Anime of the Winter
item.description: The sweet, quiet series tells a story about family and grief in a charmingly lowkey fashion.

item.title: Cassandra Kulukundis on How a Lifetime of Casting for Paul Thomas Anderson Led to ‘One Battle After Another’
item.description: Kulukundis discusses mixing movie stars, rising talent, and non-professional actors to create the most compelling and wide-ranging ensemble of Paul Thomas Anderson's career.

item.title: An Odd Weekend for Indie Film, from the Spirit Awards to an Unexpected Buy for ‘Josephine’
item.description: On this week's "Screen Talk," we also look back at all the controversy dominating news out of Berlin.

item.title: ‘Wolfram’ Review: Warwick Thornton’s ‘Sweet Country’ Follow-Up Is Just as Ravishingly Bleak
item.description: Berlin: A sequel to the 2017 film brings back familiar characters into new, and just as harrowing, scenarios.

item.description: Joachim Trier and "Fallout" will also be honored by the global film manufacturer.

item.description: Paul Gross directs himself, Leslie Nielsen, Molly Parker, and more in this wacky 2002 sports comedy.
